newsitem.title: FRANCE: French transport strike call has limited response.
newsitem.headline: French transport strike call has limited response.

text.p: A union call for a 24-hour strike in a bid to secure a shorter working-week and retirement at 55 for France's transport workers met with limited response on Tuesday, union and city authorities said.

The strike call by the Communist-led CGT union, which did not target Paris, appeared to have little or no impact in most key towns and cities, such as Lyon and Dijon in central France, Bordeaux in the southwest and Nantes in the northwest.

Transport services were severely cut back in other cities including Marseille and Toulouse in southern France, Rennes in western France and the northeastern cities of Strasbourg and Nancy, union and city authorities said.

The mixed response to the strike call came as a sign that simmering labour unrest in France would not reach last year's levels, when public sector strikes crippled the country for more than three weeks in November and December.
The strike call was inspired by the government's approval last month of retirement at 55 for French truckers, after they blocaded major highways in a 12-day protest.

Some unions say the agreement could act as a precedent. But Labour Minister Jacques Barrot told French radio on Tuesday that lowering the retirement age could jeopardise future generations' ability to pay for such a retirement system.
